# BreatheTherm

> Breathable mineral insulation for pre-1919 and listed buildings in the UK. Vapour-open lime, perlite and aerogel systems that keep solid walls drying while the home stays warm.

BreatheTherm specifies and installs vapour-open wall and floor build-ups for solid masonry. Materials are mineral and designed for listed and conservation work, including WTA 6-4 internal insulation. Contact: hello@breathetherm.co.uk, 01285 407088. The Old Forge, Todenham, Gloucestershire GL56 9PF.

Canonical pages: https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/sitemap.xml

## Start here

- [Breathable insulation for solid-wall homes](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/): Vapour-open mineral insulation for pre-1919 buildings. Cut heating bills without degrading your heritage property. Walls and floors that breathe.
- [Will it work on my house?](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/will-it-work/): Seven quick questions. A plain-English answer. No product names until you want them.
- [Book a breathable insulation assessment](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/contact/): Speak to a heritage retrofit specialist. No obligation. Clear advice tailored to your building type, age, and any conservation requirements.

## Solutions

- [Breathable insulation for solid walls](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/solutions/): Pre-1919 buildings were designed to breathe. Lime mortar, solid brick and stone absorb and release moisture as part of a natural cycle.
- [Insulating heritage listed period properties](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/solutions/internal-walls/): Breathable internal thermal upgrade to bare brick walls and a retained lath ceiling using PerliScratch, AeroBond, mesh, and PerliTherm.
- [Breathable insulation and external walls](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/solutions/external-walls/): External wall insulation on a period facade needs planning, and often listed building consent. Most BreatheTherm work is internal, so the street elevation stays as it is.
- [Breathable floor insulation](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/solutions/floors/): The insulating mineral underbase of the floor system. A vapour-open separator beneath the floor build-up.
- [Breathable insulation demo house](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/display/): Click a zone on the model to explore the build-up.

## Products

- [Breathable insulation products](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/products/): Every BreatheTherm product in its place: the breathable wall and floor build-ups, layer by layer, with typical thickness and lambda.
- [PerliTherm thermal render for solid stone walls](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/products/perlitherm/): PerliTherm perlite render. Expanded perlite bound with hydraulic lime. Thermal render for solid stone walls.
- [Breathable aerogel insulation UK](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/products/gelpanel/): An ultra-thin thermal boost where reveals and junctions are tight. Aerogel insulation UK.
- [Breathable PerliScratch sealing coat](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/products/perliscatch/): A keyed lime-perlite coat so the insulation can grip the masonry.
- [Mesh in the breathable wall lining](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/products/perlimessh/): PerliScratch, AeroBond, mesh, and PerliTherm.
- [Breathable AeroBond adhesive](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/products/aerobond/): Adhesive and basecoat in one, for aerogel and mineral layers.
- [Breathable PerliFinish finish coat](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/products/perlifinish/): A breathable lime finish, ready for decoration.
- [PerliBase floor insulation](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/products/perlibase/): The insulating mineral underbase of the floor system.
- [PerliStruct floor slab](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/products/perlistruct/): A structural lime-perlite screed that still lets vapour through.
- [PerliScreed screed layer](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/products/perlilay/): The vapour-open insulated floor finish.
- [Breathable PerliMat geotextile](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/products/perlimat/): A vapour-open separator beneath the floor build-up.

## Journal

- [Breathable insulation journal](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/guides/): Why vapour-open build-ups matter in solid masonry, and what breathable actually means on a pre-1919 wall.
- [Walls that are allowed to dry](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/guides/walls-that-are-allowed-to-dry/): Why breathable insulation matters in traditional buildings. Vapour-open lime and perlite keep solid walls drying while they get warmer in use.
- [Internal insulation and listed building consent](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/guides/internal-insulation-listed-building-consent/): Internal wall insulation on a listed building almost always needs consent. Thin vapour-open systems protect plaster, panelling and room proportions.
- [U-values without trapping moisture](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/guides/u-values-without-trapping-moisture/): Finding the balance between internal insulation and breathability. More thickness is not always safer on a solid wall that still has to dry.
- [What WTA 6-4 asks of a system](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/guides/what-wta-6-4-asks-of-a-system/): WTA 6-4 is the German guideline for internal insulation of historic walls. It judges the whole build-up, not a single material U-value on site.
- [Reading a wall before specifying thickness](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/guides/reading-a-wall-before-specifying-thickness/): Every successful solid-wall retrofit starts with the building. Survey masonry, plaster, pointing, moisture and junctions before anyone chooses millimetres.

## Projects

- [Breathable insulation projects](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/projects/): Every project is different. Every outcome is the same: a warmer, drier, healthier building that retains its heritage character.
- [Grade I Cotswold farmhouse insulation](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/projects/kerry-cottage/): Grade I Cotswold farmhouse. Solid stone, cob and lime, lined internally. U-value 0.22, bills down 52%, elevation unchanged.
- [Kerry Cottage, Perthshire: sandstone wall and floor insulation](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/projects/kerry-cottage-perthshire/): Kerry Cottage, Perthshire. 450 mm sandstone walls lined internally and a new insulated floor: 77 m² of wall, 65 m² of floor, wall U-value down 76%.
- [Did this Bristol block stay dry?](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/projects/bristol-mansion-block/): Twelve flats, every external wall lined, sensors left in the walls. Zero moisture failures at 36 months. Bills down 71%.

## Who it is for

- [Breathable insulation for homeowners](https://www.breathetherm.co.uk/for-homeowners/): Reduce energy bills and eliminate damp without compromising the character or fabric of the construction.
